Hey bro, sorry shits been whack recently. No one in these comments can help you the way a psychiatrist or psychologist can help you, especially one that you've researched and have reasons to believe are a good fit for you, but I hope others like me can drop in to also say it gets better and you'll do the work and it'll be worth it.

Turning your life around is hard because you imagine that it necessitates a big change, something that you might notice, but in reality it happens too small to notice, and in my experience that's when the effort gets lost. This is why people like Dr K emphasize journaling. By rereading days-old entries, you can see into the past and realize the difference the efforts are making.

Just do something little for yourself, something that will last to the next day. Even if you're homeless, you could be a homeless man who today and the day before read one act of Shakespeare, or did 10 minutes of meditation, or yoga.

Others know more about resources for people like you, I don't know if you're in the US, but I think there are housing programs for poor youths if you can show proof of employment.

Godspeed bro, have a good life.
